findings.text: Reviewer proved non-tautology with four one-line mutations (cap-ignoring check, plan_spend uses the global total, drop the per-spec loop, plan-level check uses the global total) each caught by the selftest and restored to 760 passed / 0 failed - exceeding the two mutations the builder claimed.

validate.py was deliberately not extended; budgets shape validation lives in budget.py.parse_budgets as a named BudgetError and check_plan ignores the unknown top-level budgets key so PLAN-0004 still validates (backward compatible). Reviewer confirmed old events and the new budgets block both parse and gate green.

summary: X5 (WARP-0405, cost and token budget governance) is correct and honest. Independent adversarial review: pass_with_notes, 0 blocking, gate GREEN (selftest 760). The reviewer drove .warp/budget.py over synthetic streams and the real CLI (under budget passes; over a plan token cap and over a per-spec cap each fail loud naming the plan or spec and the overage; a no-budgets plan passes; real PLAN-0004 exits 0 under budget), independently reimplemented the aggregation and confirmed NO DRIFT (totals and the full spend_by_correlation map equal metrics.compute() exactly; plan attribution correctly excludes unrelated correlations), and proved non-tautology with four mutations. Capabilities budget_governance=mechanical is honest (reader and enforcer plus real surface run in the gate over stdlib); both capabilities.yaml copies byte-identical; events.py and metrics.py byte-identical across both copies; backward compatible (old events and pre-budget plans still parse and gate green); proportionate (spend rides the single event stream via correlation_id, no second store or service); generic; ASCII. proof_digest recomputed via validate.py.
